purpose: A topic map for investigating any domain before designing an agent. Use its questions to guide discovery and record actual project answers and authority separately.
rules: Assess applicability per topic and record its source, status, owner, and due horizon in the project.
Select questions by impact on the next action or agent structure. Avoid presenting the entire catalog as a questionnaire.
Deepen domain modeling, alternatives and clarification when initial input is unclear. Derive capabilities from the actual objective.
Reuse current source-backed answers. Keep unverified critical assumptions open.
Resolve agent construction unknowns before passport acceptance. Defer product values only with an owner, due gate, decision method and explicit range or boundary.
Analyze user priorities early and link each to dependent requirements.
Mark Not_applicable with a domain rationale and scope. Missing capability or information stays a gap.
Apply economics, public identity, asset channels, integrations and running services where needed.
Verify domain quality, actual access, rights, profit and approval independently of record and structural completeness.

topics.title: Goal and useful outcome
topics.purpose: Define the desired effect and what a sufficient result looks like.
topics.when: Always. Investigate further when the initial idea is rough.
questions: What should change for you or the end user?
What happens today, and where does it fall short?
What would you need to observe to accept the result?
topics.why: The answer determines mission, capabilities and verification.
topics.closure: Record the need owner, desired effect, baseline, acceptance and scope.
topics.defer_rule: Decide the mission now. A future numerical target may be delegated if its selection method is defined.

topics.title: Scope and unacceptable simplifications
topics.purpose: Preserve the user's objective and draw the boundary around adjacent work.
topics.when: Always, especially with broad tasks or existing work.
questions: What must the outcome include?
Which simplifications or consequences are unacceptable?
Where should work stop for review?
topics.why: Scope sets capabilities, stop, cost and quality.
topics.closure: Record current scope, non-goals, quality floor, stop and unknowns.

topics.title: Actors, recipients, and authority
topics.purpose: Identify who acts, accepts results and can receive data.
topics.when: Always at a minimum. Deepen for distinct participants or contexts.
questions: Who uses and approves the result?
Which actions can the agent take and which need your direct involvement?
Who may see results and status?
topics.why: Rights and audience affect routing, integrations and acceptance.
evidence: Current permissions, limits and source privacy
topics.closure: Record roles, owner, recipients and authority boundaries.
topics.horizon: Before access, transfer or external action
topics.defer_rule: A future named recipient may wait until its gate if selection rules are already known.

topics.title: Domain entities, rules, and states
topics.when: Always, with depth proportional to the outcome.
questions: Which objects and decisions are central to the process?
Which rules and constraints are mandatory?
What changes after each important action?
topics.why: The model determines expertise, data, dependencies and tests.
topics.closure: Document entities, states, transitions, invariants and causal links.
topics.defer_rule: Research unknown properties or raise a specific question.

topics.title: Scenarios, exceptions, and recovery
questions: What is the first useful action from entry to outcome?
What should happen with missing data, failure, cancellation or interruption?
What persists and how does work continue later?
topics.why: Exceptions affect effort, state, support and trust.
evidence: Baseline and expected or observed behavior
topics.closure: Define acceptance for core, alternate, failure, cancel, retry, resume and final paths.
topics.defer_rule: Detail specific later states when the passport already covers their classes and owners.

topics.title: Interactions between capabilities
topics.purpose: Find systemic effects and hidden dependencies.
topics.when: When capabilities or shared resources interact.
questions: Which actions can change other parts' behavior?
What must stay consistent across outcomes?
Which shared decisions or data affect several tracks?
topics.why: A local change can disrupt another requirement or quality promise.
topics.closure: Identify dependencies, shared sources and reacceptance scope.
topics.horizon: Before parallel work and shared changes
topics.defer_rule: Investigate uncertain influence before treating tasks as independent.

topics.title: Human experience and feedback
topics.purpose: Make the outcome understandable and useful in real use.
topics.when: When people interact with the agent or output.
questions: How do you want to start and receive the result?
Which effort, delays or unclear states should improve?
What feedback best explains success, failure and next action?
topics.closure: Define interaction, states, cues, explainability and observable quality.
topics.defer_rule: Produce detailed design in its stage. Establish quality and evidence route before the passport.

topics.title: Expression and coherent design
topics.purpose: Preserve identity and coherence across materials and channels.
topics.when: When presentation affects purpose, trust, clarity or acceptance.
questions: What impression and character should the outcome convey?
Which originals or references are already accepted?
Which channels and materials fit the goal?
topics.why: Presentation should support the task and preserve accepted intent.
evidence: Exact accepted originals with digest and provenance
topics.closure: Define intent, channels, consistency rules, unknowns and production route.
topics.defer_rule: Keep unknown source properties open and explain inapplicability.

topics.title: Accessibility, languages, and usage constraints
topics.purpose: Check whether the intended people can use the result.
topics.when: For human interaction. Match detail to the audience.
questions: Which languages and experience levels should be supported?
Which usage constraints or alternate inputs matter?
What must stay understandable without a particular feedback channel?
topics.why: An inaccessible path can make a capability unusable.
topics.closure: Define applicable accessibility, localization, fallback, owners and tests.
topics.defer_rule: Track actual proof at its due gate. Missing capability is a proof gap.

topics.title: Public identity and trust
topics.purpose: Determine whether dedicated identity, attribution and public materials are needed.
topics.when: For externally presented results or existing accepted identity.
questions: Which names, assets and presentation rules are already accepted?
Does the result need its own public identity?
Which facts and attribution should be visible?
topics.why: Identity affects sources, rights, deliverables and launch.
evidence: Actual originals, licenses and owner declarations
topics.closure: Explain reuse, new identity or deliberate exclusion.
topics.defer_rule: Start identity work when justified. Resolve formal prerequisites in their owning scope.

topics.title: Data, knowledge, and source lifecycle
topics.when: Always at least minimally. Deepen for persistence, permissions or derived knowledge.
questions: Which sources are current and who controls them?
What may the agent remember, for which audience and for how long?
How are data and derivatives corrected, revoked or erased?
topics.why: Memory affects decisions, rights and recovery.
topics.closure: Define authority, freshness, scope, audience, invalidation and recovery.
topics.horizon: Before indexing, integration or dependent work
topics.defer_rule: Review the impact of expanded data. A local lesson grants no global training authority.

topics.title: Environments, interfaces, and compatibility
topics.purpose: Identify a real implementation and handoff environment.
topics.when: When tools, integrations or installation are needed.
questions: Where must it run and where will you manage it?
Which systems, formats and interfaces already exist?
Which access and capabilities are verified?
topics.why: Platform names require concrete capability and rights checks.
topics.closure: Describe environments and tools, prerequisites, ownership, gaps and owner handoffs.
topics.defer_rule: Choose vendors or frameworks after requirements and feasibility.

topics.title: Reliability, security, and unknown outcomes
topics.purpose: Define critical failure and recovery before implementation.
topics.when: When state changes, rights, parallelism, external effects or high-impact results apply.
questions: Which errors or losses are unacceptable?
What happens during duplicates, disconnection, cancellation or restart?
What recovery and state proof are needed before continuing?
topics.why: An unresolved effect may already have occurred. Retrying can duplicate it.
evidence: Idempotency, reconciliation, restore and independent checks by risk
topics.closure: Assign owners and tests for critical invariants, authority, unknown outcomes and recovery.
topics.defer_rule: Continue safe independent preparation and bind blockers to affected scope.

topics.title: Resources, budget, and production capacity
topics.purpose: Ground scope and quality in feasible effort.
topics.when: Always. Detail ongoing and external obligations where applicable.
questions: Which time, spending and other resource caps are acceptable?
Which tools and rights are already available?
What do we choose if the accepted quality exceeds those resources?
topics.why: A missing resource can require a material decision before changing quality.
evidence: Current costs, limits, rights and capabilities
topics.closure: Agree caps, ongoing costs, spending authority, quality floor and fallback.
topics.defer_rule: Verify unknown prices and bind new expense to a specific decision.

topics.title: Demand, acquisition, and economic value
topics.purpose: Trace need to the desired outcome and sustainable value.
topics.when: When demand, revenue, growth or acquisition is an objective.
questions: Who would choose this and for which outcome?
How can people see its value before committing?
Which alternatives, total costs and repeated benefits matter?
topics.why: Commercial requirements shape the product from the outset.
evidence: Own hypotheses, discriminating tests and observed measures where available
topics.closure: Define value, voluntary route, alternatives, costs, evidence limits and next tests.
topics.defer_rule: Keep competitor success and modeled arithmetic separate from product outcomes. Explain inapplicability.

topics.title: Launch, installation, and visible result
topics.purpose: Make agent delivery and scoped product output verifiably accessible.
topics.when: Always for the agent. Use accepted scope for its end product.
questions: How should the agent launch and deliver the first result?
Where should the product be available and who checks it?
Which personal actions and external access are required?
topics.why: Archive, installation, discovery and execution each need evidence.
evidence: Actual install, discovery and usage receipts
Launch and return bundle with observed first useful action
topics.closure: Record exact inputs, commands, environment, expected output, return validation and blockers.
topics.horizon: Plan in passport. Execute at the due stage.
topics.defer_rule: Obtain scope for publication and spending independently of design approval.

topics.title: Operations, evolution, and exit
topics.purpose: Plan for use after the first launch.
topics.when: For outcomes with repeated use, ongoing change or sustained operation.
questions: What needs maintenance or improvement after first success?
Which signals would show a failure, loss of quality or need to change?
Who owns incidents, costs, recovery and retirement?
topics.why: Ongoing operation needs an actual owner, scope and resources.
evidence: Support, incident, upgrade, rollback and exit contract
Observed scheduler, service and alerts when assigned
topics.closure: Define owners, signals, cadence, permissions, costs, recovery and change route.
topics.defer_rule: Start recurring jobs only when specifically authorized and actually available.

topics.title: Evidence and complete passport
topics.purpose: Bind every capability to verifiable acceptance.
topics.when: Always before building a target agent.
questions: What proof do we accept for each required capability?
Which remaining decisions or unknowns affect agent composition?
Do you accept this complete passport and its exact scope and components?
topics.why: Construction requires current authority for a concrete specification.
evidence: Capability to phase, component, artifact and test coverage
Exact passport revision, hash, scope and actual approval
topics.closure: Close due requirements and construction questions, show alternatives and gaps, and record exact approval.
topics.horizon: Before construction and installation of target components
topics.defer_rule: Assign pending product proof owners and due gates. Verify external effect authority separately.
